title: Charles H. Davis, et al. v. Presbytery of Central Georgia
disposition_detail: The Judicial Commission sustained the complaint of Charles H. Davis, et al. (Case #2) against the Presbytery of Central Georgia for not sustaining Davis's complaint against the Session of Liberty Presbyterian Church. The central adjudicated issue was the Session's closing of a disciplinary matter before any judicial action. The commission did not direct the specific relief requested by complainants (reproof of the Session, suspension from the Lord's Table, or excommunication); it requested Presbytery to aid the Session in corrections and heed WCF 24:6 and SC 87 on divorce and repentance.
first_summary: A pastor complained that Central Georgia Presbytery failed to sustain his complaint against a session that closed a disciplinary matter involving an unbiblical divorce and remarriage. The General Assembly's Judicial Commission sustained the complaint, finding that the session had closed and refused to reopen the matter before judicial action, and it requested the presbytery to aid the session in corrections and to heed confessional teaching on divorce and repentance.
summary: A teaching elder complained that Central Georgia Presbytery wrongly refused to sustain his complaint against a session that closed a disciplinary matter involving unbiblical separation, divorce, and remarriage before any judicial action. The General Assembly's Judicial Commission sustained the complaint, treating the session's "closing of the matter" as the central issue. It did not grant the requested reproof, suspension, or excommunication; it requested the presbytery to aid the session in corrections and heed WCF 24:6 and SC 87 on divorce and repentance.

sources.supports: Identifies the parties, challenged action, adopted commission judgment, grounds, and amends.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Case 2, 10th General Assembly (1982), Charles H. Davis et al. v. Presbytery of Central Georgia. The report of the Commission to hear complaints was approved and accepted as the action and judgment of the General Assembly (lines 41–43; printed p. 108).
evidence_notes.dispute: Davis complained that Presbytery wrongly refused to sustain his complaint against the Liberty Presbyterian Church Session for closing a disciplinary matter involving unbiblical separation, divorce, and remarriage before any judicial action (lines 11–33, 45; printed pp. 108–109).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The commission sustained the complaints (line 45). The central issue was the Session's "closing of the matter" (line 45). Documented grounds included counseling, session minutes closing the matter on Nov. 15, 1981, and the refusal to reopen on Nov. 18, 1981 (lines 49–55). The amends requested Presbytery to aid the Session in corrections and heed WCF 24:6 and SC 87 (lines 57–63).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The adopted report does not grant the complainants' specific petition for reproof, suspension, or excommunication; it requests aid/corrections and confessional heed. No separate opinions appear in the supplied source. Line 41 uses "Charles M. Davis" while the heading and complaint use "Charles H. Davis"; this appears to be a source variant.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: None relied on for Case #2. The report caption and line 45 also name Case #3 (David H. Bryson), but the assigned matter is Case #2 and no separate incorporated decision is needed.

source_limits: The source is a short adopted report and order, not a full opinion. It does not include the full lower-court record, hearing transcript, or separate opinions. The report caption uses "Charles M. Davis" at line 41 while the heading and complaint use "Charles H. Davis." The combined caption references Case #3 (Bryson), but the assigned matter is Case #2.
